task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello... yes, hi. I'm having a bit of trouble with my phone. I can't send picture messages — you know, the ones with photos of my grandchildren. It's been a few hours now and I just can't figure it out. Can you help me?

turns.thought: Of course — I'll do my best to help you get picture messages working again. To start, I need to pull up your account. Could you please confirm your phone number (or your full name and date of birth)?
turns.execution_output: User: Yes, of course. My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that's the right information you need...

turns.thought: Thank you, John. Let me look up your account now.

Thank you. I've located your account, John. Let me check a few things on your device. Could you please look at the very top of your phone screen — the status bar area — and tell me what you see? Or, if you'd like, I can run a diagnostic on your phone that shows that automatically. Which would you prefer?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh, um... I'm not very good at reading all those little symbols at the top. Could you just run that diagnostic thing for me? That would be much easier. Let me see if I can do it...

turns.thought:
Oh, you haven't broken anything at all — don't worry! Airplane Mode is just a setting that turns off all of your phone's wireless connections (cell service, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth). It's very easy to switch on by accident, sometimes just by tapping something on the screen. And it would definitely stop your picture messages from sending.

Let's turn it off:

1. From your home screen, **swipe downward from the very top of the screen** (start at the top edge and pull down). You may need to swipe down a second time to see all the icons.
2. Look for the **airplane icon** (✈️). If it's highlighted/colored in, it's ON.
3. **Tap the airplane icon once** so it's no longer highlighted — that turns Airplane Mode OFF.

Once you've done that, look at the top of your screen again: you should now see signal bars (like 📶) and possibly "5G" or "LTE" instead of the airplane icon.

Can you do that and tell me what you see in the status bar afterwards?
turns.execution_output: User: All right, let me try... I'm swiping down from the top like you said. I see the little airplane picture. I'm tapping it now.

turns.thought:
You did everything right, and your photos are perfectly safe — I promise. Nothing is lost.

"No Signal" and "Data Disabled" are just two more settings we need to sort out. Let me have you take the next step, and let me check something on my end as well.

**Please do this on your phone:**

1. Go to **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (on some phones it's called **Connections** or **Mobile network**).
3. Look for **Mobile data** (sometimes just called **Data**) and make sure the switch is **ON**.

While you do that, let me run a check on your phone from my side.

You did everything right — turning Airplane Mode off was the correct step, and your photos are completely safe. Nothing gets deleted when Airplane Mode is on or off; the photos stay right where they are on your phone. Any picture message that didn't go through just sits in your messaging app waiting to be sent again.

Two things showed up now, and we'll handle them one at a time.

**1. "Data Disabled"**

This is a separate on/off switch for mobile data on your phone. Let's turn it back on:

- Open the **Settings** app on your phone (the icon that looks like a gear ⚙️).
- Tap **Network & internet** (on some phones it's called **Connections**).
- Tap **Mobile network** (or **SIMs**).
- Find the switch called **Mobile data** and tap it so it's ON.

Picture messages need mobile data to send, so this is important.

**2. "No Signal"**

Right after turning Airplane Mode off, phones sometimes take a little while — usually 30 seconds or so — to reconnect to the network. So this may simply sort itself out.

Could you turn mobile data on, wait about 30 seconds, and then tell me what you see at the top of your screen? I'm especially hoping to see signal bars and something like "5G" or "LTE" appear.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, I'll try. Settings... gear thing... Network and internet... Mobile network... I see "Mobile data." Tapping it now.

turns.thought:
I understand, and I'm sorry this has been frustrating — you've been very patient. Let me keep digging into this for you.

I'm going to run a couple of quick checks directly, if you'll bear with me one more moment.

I understand — that's genuinely frustrating, and I'm sorry you've been at this a while. But no, I don't think your phone is broken. From my end, your line looks perfectly healthy: it's Active, there's no suspension, no billing issue, and you've used 8.7 GB of your 15 GB plan, so you have plenty of data left. That tells me the problem is a setting on the phone itself, which is fixable.

Since mobile data still shows "Disabled" even after you turned it on in Settings, the phone probably just needs a fresh start to pick up the new settings. Let's try the simplest thing first:

**Restart your phone:**
1. **Press and hold the power button** on the side of your phone (on some phones it's the power button plus the volume-down button together).
2. Hold it until a menu appears on the screen.
3. Tap **Restart** (if you don't see "Restart," tap **Power off**, wait about 10 seconds, then press and hold the power button again to turn it back on).
4. Wait for the phone to fully start back up — this can take a minute or two.

Once it's back on, **wait about 30 seconds**, then look at the top of your screen again.

I'm hoping you'll now see signal bars and something like "5G", "LTE", or "4G". Could you restart it and tell me what you see afterwards?

If there's still no signal after the restart, we'll try reconnecting the SIM card — the small card inside the phone that connects you to our network. I'll walk you through that step by step, and if we can't get there, I'll make sure you get handed to someone with more specialized tools who can dig in deeper.

You've been very patient, and I'm sorry this is dragging on. First and most importantly: **your photos are completely safe.** Photo messages don't get deleted when they fail to send — they sit in your messaging app, ready to go the moment we get your connection working. Nothing on your phone has been erased.

About the SIM: it's a tiny card inside your phone that connects you to our network, and I only ever recommend it as a last step. We're not at that point, and you won't need to take anything out of your phone.

I have good news about your account: your line is **Active**, there's no suspension, and you've used only 8.7 GB of your 15 GB plan — so nothing on our end is blocking you. The issue is in the phone's connection settings, and I've run out of tools on my side to diagnose it further. I'm going to hand you to a specialist who can run deeper checks on your line and device.

Let me connect you now so you don't lose your place in the queue.
